entryPoint: SLA::priorityEscalation() — public, zero-argument instance method in include/class.sla.php (line 116-118). This is the facade surface callers use to ask whether a given SLA plan should escalate ticket priority.
coreLogic: The entire method body is one expression: `return $this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE;` (include/class.sla.php:117). `$this->flags` is the SLA's persisted integer bitmask instance property, hydrated by the ORM (VerySimpleModel) from the `ost_sla.flags` column (schema default 3 = FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE). `self::FLAG_ESCALATE` is the class constant 0x0002 (include/class.sla.php:28). This line uses PHP's logical AND (`&&`), NOT the bitwise AND (`&`) used by every sibling flag-check in the same class: getInfo() line 77 (`$this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE`), isActive() line 91, isTransient() line 95, hasFlag() line 103. Because FLAG_ESCALATE (2) is a nonzero constant it is always truthy, so the expression algebraically reduces to `(bool) $this->flags` — it returns true whenever ANY bit is set (e.g. FLAG_ACTIVE alone, with the escalate bit OFF, still returns true) and false only when flags === 0. There is no delegation chain below this method; it calls nothing else, so the 'core logic' is this single expression itself.
consumers: No call sites for SLA::priorityEscalation() exist anywhere in this codebase today. Exhaustive grep across include/, scp/, api/, plugins/, and orchestrator/ found zero real callers besides its own definition; the only other textual match is an illustrative example string inside orchestrator/agents/extractor.ts's prompt (not a real call site). The method is effectively unused/dead in the current live call graph.

Indirectly related consumers read/write the SAME flags bit via separate, independently-implemented paths that must NOT be touched by this extraction: SLA::getInfo() (include/class.sla.php:74-79) computes `enable_priority_escalation` via the CORRECT bitwise `&` and is consumed by include/staff/slaplan.inc.php:9 (`$info = $sla->getInfo();`) to prefill the admin SLA-plan edit form's `$info` array (note: the rendered form in slaplan.inc.php has no visible checkbox for this field today).

SLA::update($vars, &$errors) (include/class.sla.php:145-213) reads `$vars['enable_priority_escalation']` and OR's it into `$this->flags` before save() (line 191); it is invoked from scp/slas.php line 30 (`$sla->update($_POST,$errors)` on POST do=update) and line 41 (`$_sla->update($_POST, $errors)` on POST do=add).
inputShape: No parameters. Called on an already-instantiated, already-hydrated SLA ORM object (e.g. via SLA::lookup($id) or SLA::objects()); reads only the instance property $this->flags, an integer already loaded from the ost_sla.flags column by the ORM before this method runs. No by-reference parameters, no arguments of any kind.
outputShape: Boolean, produced by PHP's `&&` operator over `$this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE`. Truth table given FLAG_ESCALATE=2 (always truthy): flags == 0 -> false; flags != 0 (ANY bit set, not necessarily the escalate bit) -> true. This is NOT equivalent to `(flags & FLAG_ESCALATE) != 0` — e.g. flags=1 (FLAG_ACTIVE only, escalation OFF per getInfo()'s own bitwise definition) still returns true from this method. No object is created or mutated; single scalar boolean returned by value.
sideEffects: None inside priorityEscalation() itself: it issues no DB read/write — it only reads the in-memory $this->flags property, which must already be hydrated on the SLA instance from a prior ORM fetch.
No global state is read or written ($cfg or otherwise).
No lazy-loading is triggered (unlike getSchedule() on the same class, which lazily loads $this->_schedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup()).
No caching, no file I/O, no Signal::send(), no logging inside this method.

Context only (NOT to be ported into the extracted service): SLA::update() has real side effects on the same flags column — Format::htmlchars(), Signal::send('object.edited', ...), and $this->save() (ORM UPDATE plus $this->updated = SqlFunction::NOW()). These belong to the update()/getInfo() call paths, not to priorityEscalation().
constraints: Preserve the exact `&&` (logical) operator from the original — do NOT 'correct' it to bitwise `&` even though FLAG_ESCALATE's name, getInfo()'s equivalent field, and every sibling flag-check method in this class (isActive, isTransient, hasFlag) use bitwise `&`. Parity requires bug-for-bug behavioral equivalence, not the presumably-intended behavior.

Return type must remain the boolean produced by `&&` (true/false), not the raw masked integer a bitwise `&` would produce (e.g. getInfo()'s enable_priority_escalation is an int 0 or 2, not a bool) — method signature and return type must be unchanged per the ticket.

The extracted service must never call SLA::priorityEscalation() itself (anti-recursion) — lift the exact `$flags && FLAG_ESCALATE` expression into the new service rather than forward-delegating back to the facade entry point being replaced.

No new DB query, global read, or lazy-load may be introduced. The extracted method must accept the already-hydrated flags value (or the SLA instance) and operate purely in-memory, exactly like the original.

Do not modify getInfo(), update(), isActive(), isTransient(), hasFlag(), or the FLAG_* constants — same class/bitmask family as MOD-1 but out of scope for this seam; only priorityEscalation()'s body may change, and only to delegate.
FLAG_ESCALATE = 0x0002 must be referenced from the SLA class (constant or passed-in value), not duplicated as a bare literal in the new service, to avoid drift if the constant ever changes.

There are zero current callers of priorityEscalation() in-tree; the strangler patch must not add, remove, or change any caller — it only changes the method body from an inline expression to a delegating call.

ost_sla.flags schema default is 3 (int(10) unsigned NOT NULL default 3 = FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE) — parity fixtures should include this real-world default value in addition to the required enabled/disabled/zero cases.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single integer field `flags` — the raw bitmask value to set on a transient/stub SLA instance before invoking priorityEscalation(). Suggested scenario values: 0 = no flags set (required edge case), 1 = FLAG_ACTIVE only (escalation intentionally OFF per getInfo()'s bitwise definition — this is the case that exposes the legacy && vs & bug, since it still returns true), 2 = FLAG_ESCALATE only (escalation enabled, not active), 3 = FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ESCALATE (the real-world schema default, escalation enabled). The harness returns `{"output": <bool>}`, the exact value SLA::priorityEscalation() returns for that flags value, to be diffed bit-for-bit against the strangler-patched version.
